 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. Celtic will look to bounce back from their recent European defeat as they travel away from home to face Hibernian in their next Scottish Premiership match on Sunday. 
 Hibernian vs Celtic – Match preview and team news
 Date: Sunday, 25th October.
 Kick-off: 1pm BST.
 Venue: Easter Road Stadium, Edinburgh.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Hibernian team news
 Hibernian face a severe squad depletion with up to seven first-team players ruled out as manager Marink Reedijk chases his elusive first home league victory.
 The most recent setback is Callum Wright, who is sidelined for a few weeks due to a groin injury sustained in training. He joins a lengthy injury list that includes Nathan Lowe with a back problem, Kanayo Megwa managing a thigh strain, and Rocky Bushiri recovering from an Achilles issue.
 Furthermore, Jordan Obita remains out with a calf complaint, alongside Jacob Devaney. On a more positive note, the Hibees are boosted by the recent returns of Adam Mayor and Jamie McGrath, both of whom successfully rejoined the matchday squad last week against Falkirk.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Additionally, winger Rabbi Matondo is heavily pushing for his first start for the club following several impactful appearances off the substitutes' bench.
 Celtic team news
 Celtic receive a substantial defensive lift ahead of the trip to Easter Road, with manager Martin O'Neill welcoming back key pillars Cameron Carter-Vickers and Alistair Johnston.
 Both defenders have resumed full training and are expected to slide straight back into the squad following recent absences. Domestically, the manager's options are further strengthened by the availability of Jota, Landon Emenalo, and Shim Mheuka, all of whom return to the selection pool after being ineligible for the midweek European tie against Celta Vigo.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Meanwhile, Callum Osmand is fit to feature; O'Neill confirmed his forced substitution during the European match was merely due to a precautionary cramp.
 The only persistent concern for the league leaders surrounds winger Yang Hyun-jun, who remains a major doubt for the lunchtime kick-off as he continues his recovery from a lingering hamstring issue.
 Form
 Hibernian
 Hibernian endure a miserable run of form, languishing at the bottom of the table in 12th place. The Hibees have struggled for consistency under Marink Reedijk, suffering five defeats in their last six Premiership outings. Their defensive vulnerability remains a core issue, having failed to keep a single clean sheet all season. Recent results include a tight 1-0 away loss to Dundee United followed by a frustrating 2-1 defeat at Easter Road against Falkirk last weekend.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Celtic
 Celtic dominate the domestic landscape, sitting comfortably at the summit of the Scottish Premiership. Martin O'Neill's clinical side has secured 15 victories from their last 16 league fixtures. Domestically, the league leaders bounce into this game following a comprehensive 2-0 win over Motherwell and a ruthless 7-1 thrashing of Hearts. However, they are looking to recover from a minor blip after suffering a midweek 2-1 loss to Celta Vigo in Europe.
 Predicted lineups
 Hibernian: Sallinger; Passlack, Kerr, Ivezic, Mayor; Mulligan, Chaiwa; Boyle, McGrath, Klidje; Elding
 Celtic: Sinisalo; Donovan, Murray, Scales, Tierney; Baur, McGregor; Hassan, Nygren, Forrest; Duran
